title.title: A ZFC counterexample to Naimark's problem
title.subtitle: Claim: in ZFC, a simple non-elementary C*-algebra whose irreducible representations are all equivalent

beats.text: Algebras with one irreducible representation, and the elementary ones $K(H)$
Separable: they coincide (Rosenberg 1953). Assuming $\diamondsuit$ they differ (2004)
Claim: in plain ZFC, a simple nonseparable example with a faithful trace

achievement.label: Naimark's problem (1948)
achievement.context: Before: true for separable algebras (Rosenberg 1953); false assuming $\diamondsuit$ (Akemann–Weaver 2004)
achievement.note: Not first: Tanaka's ZFC example appeared two days earlier

verify.detail: The ZFC counterexample, over Hilbert spaces in arbitrary universes
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with the claim; we did not build it

plain: An algebra with just one way to act irreducibly, yet unlike the standard example; built without extra axioms

steps: Build the algebra in a long, uncountable sequence of steps
Each step adds a bridge that makes old pure states equivalent
Unique extensions keep earlier states intact along the way

voice.text: Separable examples are always the compact operators. Extra set theory gave a strange exception.
Build it in uncountably many steps, each making old pure states equivalent.
Claimed: one exists using only standard axioms.
